previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient, a woman with T1-T2 paraplegia, COPD, and a history of recurrent pneumonias, was admitted for hypoxia, respiratory distress, and somnolence following a recent hospital discharge. She presented with tachypnea, increased oxygen needs, and hypercapnia, requiring BIPAP and ICU monitoring. Imaging showed bibasilar atelectasis and right lower lobe consolidation, concerning for aspiration pneumonia. She was treated with cefepime and vancomycin for suspected hospital-acquired pneumonia. A PICC line was placed for outpatient antibiotic completion but required repositioning due to malplacement. Sedating medications including clonazepam were held, and baclofen was reduced to mitigate oversedation and aspiration risk. A swallowing study showed no aspiration, allowing diet advancement. She improved clinically, remained afebrile with negative blood and urine cultures, and was discharged home with services for three additional days of IV antibiotics. Medication adjustments included discontinuation of clonazepam, reduced baclofen, and transition to ranitidine and lower-dose nicotine patch.

CLINICAL HISTORY:  ___ woman with decreased oxygen saturation to 84%
at home, history of recent pneumonia, assess for residual/recurrent pneumonia.

FINDINGS:  AP and lateral views of the chest were obtained.  There is
persistent bibasilar lung opacity which likely represents persistent
consolidation which is overall stable from prior exam.  There may be slight
decrease in right-sided pleural effusion compared with the prior exam.  Heart
size appears grossly stable.  Bony structures are demineralized with extensive
ribcage deformity and hardware noted at both shoulders.

IMPRESSION:  Persistent right and left lower lung opacities concerning for
ongoing infectious process.  Slight improvement in right pleural effusion. 
Would recommend followup to resolution.

HISTORY:  ___ woman with persistent right-sided opacity, hypoxia and
fever, evaluate for infectious etiology versus additional findings given
minimal improvement despite broad-spectrum antibiotics.

CT CHEST:  Axial imaging was performed from the thoracic inlet through the
upper abdomen after uneventful administration of intravenous contrast. 
Sagittal and coronal reformatted images were prepared.

COMPARISON:  Multiple prior chest CT examinations, most recent from ___.

FINDINGS:  Incidental note is again made of an azygos fissure and lobe. 
Bibasilar atelectasis with mild mucoid impaction on the right is little
changed.  Ground-glass opacity in the inferior segment of the right upper lobe
(2:34) appears stable to slightly improved.  Trace bilateral pleural effusions
are present.  Along the right posterior mediastinum (2:37) is a 2.7 mm
intermediate density mass present on prior examinations although may have
slightly increased in size over the past ___ years.  There is a small
pericardial effusion.  Heart and great vessels otherwise appear normal.  No
significant axillary or hilar lymphadenopathy is present.  The lobes of the
thyroid appear normal.  There is a stable calcified left pericardial lymph
node (2:34).

BONE WINDOWS:  There is bilateral fixation hardware within the humeral heads. 
There are multiple bilateral chronic rib deformities causing deformation of
the chest wall.

Limited views of the upper abdomen appear grossly normal.

IMPRESSION:

1.  No significant change in bibasilar atelectasis with improved aeration
particularly at the right base.

2.  Minimal increased enlargement of a right posterior mediastinal mass, which
may be a lymph node or other nonaggressive entity such as neurogenic tumor,
over approximately a nine-year period.

3.  Bilateral humeral head fixation hardware and bilateral chronic rib
fractures stable.
